article.title: Titanium Over Traditional Option
article.author: Sejal Desai
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Men approach jewellery with great consideration of compatibility with what they always do. That’s the short answer to the curiosity behind the preference for titanium rings. Those who always get dirt on their hands or have to work with harsh machinery know that their job can easily destroy an expensive soft gold band within weeks. But if that isn’t enough reason to convince, here’s a list of more rationale behind the shift to this particular metal. Scratch and Dent Resistance As we pointed out, gold is soft. It’s one of the reasons why they work well in fine jewellery. However, it’s also the reason why they easily pick up dents and scratches from daily manual work. Just seeing it withstand the test of time doesn’t mean it’s durable in any practical sense. You buy them with hopes they’d stay pristine. By choosing mens titanium rings , wearers don’t have to worry about visible damage. They hold their finish under conditions that would visibly damage gold and other traditional metals. The sturdiness of titanium jewellery resists small impacts or scratches when working with rough materials. Give it a year and the titanium piece stays close to how it looked on day one. This is something you cannot say about gold or silver bands. Weight That Doesn’t Interfere With Grip or Dexterity A heavy ring becomes a genuine hindrance for anyone whose hands need to move precisely and repeatedly through a working day. Let’s say platinum, in particular. This material is dense enough to make it heavier to the finger. Men who use a lot of their hands for work would find it very distracting. Titanium is lighter than platinum and other traditional jewellery materials. A ring made out of it can be worn with a solid, substantial profile without adding the weight that a similarly sized ring in a traditional metal would carry. So if you plan to work without having a repeated look at your ring finger, titanium should be your choice of metal for a wedding band. Corrosion Resistance Against Oil, Sweat, and Chemical Exposure Cleaning chemicals and engine oil, even fluid as simple as sweat, can cause tarnishing on jewellery. Silver is vulnerable under this kind of exposure, and some gold alloys can react with some chemicals that cause them to lose their finish over time. Meanwhile, titanium resists corrosion from most chemicals that you can see in workplaces and households. It doesn’t react with sweat and most industrial chemicals either. If you worry too much about discolouration due to exposure to chemicals and your own sweat, titanium shields itself from that kind of chemical degradation. A Safety Profile Better Than Traditional Metals This is the reason that carries the most weight for men working around machinery. A ring caught on rotating equipment or heavy tools can cause serious injury. Sometimes, the wearer is at the mercy of the way a metal responds to a catastrophic force. Standard titanium rings are engineered to bend or break under extreme force. This is a good safety consideration for men working around power tools and heavy machinery. If needed, they can be torn away from the wearer's body by professionals and emergency respondents using the right tools. Meanwhile, gold or platinum bands are more malleable. They will deform and constrict on the wearer at times when you don’t need them to. Durability That Justifies the Cost Over a Working Lifetime A gold band that gets scratched, dented, and eventually needs resizing or repolishing carries an ongoing cost most buyers don’t factor in at the point of purchase. Titanium’s resistance to scratching and denting means a well-made titanium ring can be worn daily for decades without needing the kind of maintenance that softer metals require. For a man who’s going to wear the same ring through years of manual work, the upfront cost comparison against gold or platinum misses the point. The relevant comparison is what the ring looks like, and costs to maintain, five or ten years into daily wear. On that measure, titanium consistently comes out ahead for anyone whose hands don’t get an easy day at the office.
